terra.problem: The delegation goes to Isaiah, but the text does not say they show up at his door.
“Wrong door” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
The text does not say that nobody is waving anything.
The explanation is flat and repeats the same distinction without adding insight or personality.
“Hezekiah has barely finished worrying” adds an unmarked feeling and a timing the text does not give.
The text does not establish that nobody boards a boat anywhere in the story.
“He’s got a new worry” attributes a feeling to Sennacherib without marking it as a guess.
Hezekiah has already made requests before verse 17, asking the LORD to hear and see in verse 16.
“If hands made it, a fire can finish it” makes an unsupported general claim, including about objects made of stone.
“Sennacherib was loud for a long time” adds a duration the passage does not give.
The text does not say Sennacherib thought he had done it all on his own.
“He gets led out” presents the LORD’s hook-and-bit imagery as a literal event. The text later says Sennacherib withdrew.
Exodus 12:51 says the LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt; it does not support the stated fact that Moses led them out.
